headline: Los Angeles County supervisors are due to consider a motion to draft a ban on large AI data centers in the county's unincorporated areas.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: a large county's proposed ban with a clear vote date, but only a proposal to start drafting.
importance_line: Residents of unincorporated LA County communities would be spared very large data centers and developers shut out, but Tuesday's step only starts the drafting of a rule, and the outcome of the vote is not yet known.
summary: The Los Angeles Daily News reports that the Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors is due to consider on Tuesday 6 Oct 2026 a motion by Supervisor Hilda Solis directing planners to draft a zoning rule that would ban large-scale AI data centers in every zone of the unincorporated areas (those outside city limits), citing energy and water demand and possible health effects. Several nearby cities, including Monterey Park, Montebello, Baldwin Park and El Monte, have already acted to restrict or halt data center projects, and the motion also asks the county to study whether its noise rules cover the continuous low-pitched noise these facilities make.
notes: A proposal, not an action: the Tuesday vote had not happened when the article ran. Background in the motion: the planning director's interim prohibition of 17 Sep 2026 and the county study begun in April.
